Ammonia, in particular, poses significant toxicity concerns, and would require careful management to mitigate risks. However, renewable diesel should be handled like traditional diesel. Alternative fuels have the potential to reduce lifecycle air pollutants and criteria emissions, but risk assessments may be needed to ensure safe implementation and avoid operational hazards. ES.6 FUTURE DIRECTIONS Coordinated efforts are needed across railroads, owners-operators, engine manufacturers, alternative fuel producers, and researchers to diversify energy sources and strengthen energy security in the rail sector. To overcome economic barriers and support adoption, it is crucial to strengthen federal and state cooperation, invest in infrastructure, scale up the volumes of available alternative fuel technologies, and foster stakeholder engagement. Continued research, development, and demonstrations are needed to improve efficiency and reduce the costs associated with engine modifications and alternative fuel production. In addition, more research and technology demonstrations are required to produce a higher volume of alternative fuels using domestic feedstocks to increase overall energy security. In conclusion, this report provides a comprehensive assessment of alternative fuels for the rail sector, offering insights into their potential to satisfy consumer demands, tap into additional energy sources, and improve the economics and efficiency of rail movement.
